method_note: FAST mode, one round. WebFetch could not resolve thuvienphapluat.vn or smartraveller.gov.au in this session (network allowlist). Apify web-fetch timed out once. facts.claim: An Australian citizen, or a citizen of another country domiciled in Australia, who intends to marry in Vietnam must include a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) in the marriage application submitted to Vietnamese authorities. The page states that it is the Vietnamese government that has the authority to solemnise marriages in Vietnam, and that the couple still needs to marry after the CNI is issued.
facts.publisher: Australian Consulate-General, Ho Chi Minh City (DFAT)
facts.source_date: CNI procedure document linked from the page is dated 17 Sep 2020
facts.authority: DFAT, Australian Consulate-General Ho Chi Minh City
facts.use_note: The page does not mention residency rules, legalisation or Apostille.

facts.claim: Law on Civil Status 2014 (Law 60/2014/QH13, in force 1 Jan 2016), Article 37(2): where a foreigner residing in Vietnam (nguoi nuoc ngoai cu tru tai Viet Nam) requests marriage registration in Vietnam, the district-level People's Committee where either party resides registers the marriage. Article 37(1) covers a Vietnamese citizen marrying a foreigner (district People's Committee where the Vietnamese citizen resides).
facts.publisher: Thu Vien Phap Luat (text of law, as quoted)
facts.authority: National Assembly of Vietnam (Law 60/2014/QH13); registration by People's Committee
facts.use_note: Read from search snippets only; thuvienphapluat.vn could not be fetched in this session and the official vbpl.vn text was not reached. The wording consistently ties registration between foreigners to residence in Vietnam. No official provision was found that lets two foreigners who do not reside in Vietnam register a marriage there. Do not state a definitive 'yes'. See F-005 and needs N-001.

facts.claim: Under Article 4 of Decree 120/2025/ND-CP (effective 1 Jul 2025, two-tier local government), commune-level People's Committees (xa, phuong, dac khu) exercise civil status registration powers under Chapter III of the Law on Civil Status 2014, and the tasks formerly held by the district People's Committee and its chair pass to the commune-level People's Committee and its chair. District-level People's Committees no longer register marriages.
facts.publisher: Ha Tinh Provincial Portal, reprinting Bao Chinh phu (Government newspaper)
facts.authority: Government of Vietnam, Decree 120/2025/ND-CP; registering body is the commune-level People's Committee
facts.use_note: Supersedes the 'district People's Committee' wording in Article 37 of the 2014 Law. The writer should say commune or ward People's Committee, not district.

facts.claim: Decree 120/2025/ND-CP: the processing time for registering a marriage with a foreign element is 5 working days from receipt of a complete and valid dossier; where verification is needed it may be extended but not beyond 10 working days.
facts.publisher: Ha Tinh Provincial Portal, reprinting Bao Chinh phu
facts.use_note: Processing time only. Not a statement of total lead time including document preparation.

facts.claim: Decree 120/2025/ND-CP: where the competent commune-level People's Committee cannot be identified, or the person requesting civil status registration has no place of residence in Vietnam, the provincial Department of Justice (So Tu phap) receives the request and within 2 working days reports to the provincial People's Committee chair, or assigns a suitable commune-level People's Committee, and guides the person on where to file.
facts.publisher: Ha Tinh Provincial Portal, reprinting Bao Chinh phu
facts.authority: Government of Vietnam, Decree 120/2025/ND-CP; provincial Department of Justice
facts.use_note: This is a general routing rule for civil status requests, not a marriage-specific grant of eligibility. It does not override the residence wording in Law on Civil Status Article 37(2) (F-002). The two sources point in different directions for non-resident foreign couples, so confidence is low. Use only to say: contact the provincial Department of Justice to confirm. Never use it to tell readers that two non-residents can marry legally in Vietnam.

facts.claim: Vietnam has acceded to the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961 Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (Apostille Convention). The Convention entered into force for Vietnam on 11 September 2026. From that date, public documents between Vietnam and Contracting Parties for which the Convention is in force with Vietnam need only a single Apostille certificate in place of consular legalisation.
facts.publisher: Consulate General of Viet Nam in Shanghai (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Viet Nam)
facts.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Viet Nam
facts.use_note: This overturns the run-log assumption that Vietnam is not an Apostille member. Australia is a Contracting Party, but whether the Convention applies between Australia and Vietnam (no objection lodged) was not confirmed from the HCCH status table in this round. See N-002.

facts.claim: A public document bearing a valid Apostille may be used in Viet Nam without any further certification. Where the document is not drawn up in Vietnamese, a Vietnamese translation, notarised or certified in accordance with the law of Viet Nam, is required.
facts.publisher: Consulate General of Viet Nam in Shanghai (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Viet Nam)
facts.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Viet Nam
facts.use_note: Notice is written for Chinese documents but states the general rule. Safe to state the translation rule generally.

facts.claim: Documents legalised through consular channels before 11 September 2026 remain valid for use in Viet Nam with no need to obtain an Apostille instead; Apostilles issued by foreign competent authorities before 11 September 2026 are also accepted.
facts.publisher: Consulate General of Viet Nam in Shanghai (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Viet Nam)
facts.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Viet Nam

facts.claim: Decree 293/2026/ND-CP, issued 23 July 2026 and effective 11 September 2026, implements the Apostille Convention in Vietnam. Agencies receiving documents in Vietnam may not require any further consular certification or legalisation for documents that already carry an Apostille. Documents made by diplomatic or consular officers are excluded from the Apostille exemption (Article 11).
facts.publisher: So Tu phap Can Tho (Can Tho Department of Justice), legal education portal
facts.use_note: The exclusion of documents made by diplomatic or consular officers matters: a CNI issued by an Australian embassy or consulate officer may fall outside the Apostille route, while one issued by DFAT in Australia would not. Not confirmed for CNIs specifically. See N-003.

facts.claim: Vietnamese public documents are submitted for an Apostille to the competent authority in Vietnam (Vietnam's consulates abroad do not issue Apostilles). Information on the receiving authority, documents, fees and processing time is published at apostille.lanhsuvietnam.gov.vn.
facts.publisher: Consulate General of Viet Nam in Shanghai (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Viet Nam)
facts.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Viet Nam
facts.use_note: Relevant when a Vietnamese marriage certificate is taken back to Australia.

facts.claim: Marriage and Family Law 2014, Article 8(1): to marry, a man must be fully 20 years of age or older and a woman fully 18 or older; marriage must be voluntary and the parties must not have lost civil act capacity.
facts.publisher: Thu Vien Phap Luat (text of law, as quoted)
facts.use_note: From search snippets only; page could not be fetched. Consistent across multiple results.

facts.claim: Marriage and Family Law 2014, Article 8(2): the State does not recognise marriage between persons of the same sex.
facts.publisher: Thu Vien Phap Luat (text of law, as quoted)
facts.use_note: From search snippets only. Write as 'not recognised', not 'banned'.

facts.claim: Smartraveller's Vietnam marriage notes (as summarised in search results) say a CNI from DFAT must be authenticated by the Vietnamese embassy or consulate in Australia before Vietnam's Department of Justice will recognise it.
facts.use_note: Could not fetch the page (host blocked in this session); seen only in search summary. Likely predates Vietnam's Apostille accession (F-006, F-009), so it conflicts with current Vietnamese rules for any document issued in Australia after 11 Sep 2026. Do not publish either version as settled until N-002 and N-003 are resolved.

needs.question: Can two foreigners who do not reside in Vietnam register a marriage there? Official sources found tie registration between foreigners to residence in Vietnam (F-002); Decree 120/2025 routes requesters with no residence to the provincial Department of Justice (F-005) without saying marriage is available to them. Needs written confirmation from a provincial Department of Justice (So Tu phap, e.g. Ha Noi, Ho Chi Minh City, Da Nang, Khanh Hoa) or the Australian Embassy Hanoi consular section. Also fetch the official Article 37 text from vbpl.vn.
